priya: Heads-up: I opened a Terraform PR to change the per-model configmap keys (adding perf_tweaks + small_rerank: true) and to move the api token reference out of the configmap into a Secret ref. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/512
ben: Nice. FYI updating a ConfigMap in k8s won't force pods to restart. If your app doesn't watch files, nothing will change until a rollout. We usually use an annotation on the deployment template to trigger a rolling update when the config changes.
theo: Two quick approaches:
- compute a checksum/hash of the rendered config and put it under spec.template.metadata.annotations.checksum/config
- use a small post-apply step in CI that kubectl rolls restart or patches the deployment timestamp
Example TF snippet we use:
```
locals {
  rendered = templatefile("./model-config.tpl", { data = var.model_map })
  cfg_hash = md5(local.rendered)
}
resource "kubernetes_deployment" "svc" {
  spec {
    template {
      metadata {
        annotations = {
          "checksum/config" = local.cfg_hash
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
sasha: Re: secrets: do NOT put secret values in ConfigMaps. Having the secret name in a ConfigMap is fine as a pointer, but prefer using secretKeyRef or projected volumes so k8s secrets lifecycle is respected. Example env var:
```
- name: MODEL_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: model-keys
      key: prod_key
```
priya: Good — I already switched to secretKeyRef in the PR. One question: our deployment is managed by ArgoCD; will changing the configmap+annotation via Terraform cause Argo to revert? Any pitfalls?
ben: If ArgoCD is the source of truth for k8s manifests, applying changes via TF directly can fight with Argo. Two patterns:
- Let Argo manage the deployment and configmap, have TF update the Git repo (or commit the rendered config) so Argo picks it up.
- Or have TF only manage the ConfigMap and then trigger Argo sync for the kustomize/helm app. Avoid two controllers changing the same object without coordination.
theo: Another option: use a small sidecar like stakater/Reloader or configmap-reload which watches the mounted configmap and sends SIGHUP to the main process. That avoids rolling restarts but requires app support. Also works well with Argo since you change only the ConfigMap.
sasha: Also check RBAC for the pod's service account: if your pod reads secrets, the SA needs secrets/get. We've seen a case where a non-prod namespace SA couldn't read secrets after migration.
priya: Great call. I'll add a ticket to audit SA permissions across model namespaces.
ops-bot: [ci/status] terraform plan for infra/keptn: ok  waiting for approval.
deploy-bot: Note: if you're planning a rollout during traffic spikes, coordinate with eng-oncall. (auto msg)
but ben: Small nuance: if the config contains large blobs (e.g., 100s of model-specific flags), computing md5 of the entire file can be noisy. Consider hashing only keys that affect runtime (exclude comments/metadata). We use jsonencode(var.model_map) then md5 that output.
priya: Thanks — I'll update the TF to use jsonencode and md5, and I'll switch the CI patch to call `kubectl -n services patch deploy model-svc -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"reloadedAt":"'$(date +%s)'"}}}}}'` as a fallback for Argo-managed apps.
ben: lgtm. Ping me for a quick review after you push changes.
priya: Will do, thanks!
